question: Can a single-host append-only job ledger resume the preferred Blender 5.2 production compiler after orchestrator loss and a controlled native-Blender interruption without trusting mutable state, losing accepted evidence, or rerunning a completed immutable stage?

capacityAtPreregistration.formalExecutionRule: If a fresh preflight or any native-spawn JIT readmission falls below the unchanged reserve, stop before Blender and recover capacity; never lower or override the threshold.

included: orchestrator process exits after a durable completed-stage receipt and before the next stage begins
native Blender receives a controlled termination during an incomplete compile attempt
a restarted orchestrator encounters a live matching process and must not duplicate it
ledger, manifest, receipt, artifact and resource-accounting mutation
PID reuse or unverifiable process identity causing fail-closed recovery
excluded: filesystem corruption or loss of acknowledged fsync writes
network filesystems and concurrent external writers
power-loss durability beyond the local filesystem contract

jobContract.stateAuthority: Only an immutable manifest plus a contiguous append-only hash-chained event ledger and verified immutable stage receipts may determine recovery state; a mutable status file is never authoritative.
durability: exclusive-create every manifest, event and terminal receipt
fsync the containing directory after creation
never rewrite, truncate, rename over or delete accepted evidence

stageDag.completedBy: a valid immutable plan receipt binding two byte-identical BuildPlan compilations
a valid B57 production receipt plus independently valid current CompileReceipt and native disk admission
the preferred verifier's valid result bound to the production receipt bytes
a self-hashed final receipt binding the complete ledger, stage receipts, artifacts and resource totals

recoveryRules.completedStage: Verify the ledger prefix, stage receipt self-hash, declared input/output hashes, artifact roster and stage-specific verifier; then emit SKIPPED_VERIFIED without spawning that stage again.
recoveryRules.startedWithoutTerminalReceipt: Check the recorded process identity. If the exact process is live, return WAIT_LIVE_PROCESS and spawn nothing. If it is dead, unverifiable or identity-mismatched, write a non-promotable abandonment receipt and retry only in a new empty attempt root.
recoveryRules.failedStage: Preserve the failed attempt, mark it non-promotable and retry only the failed stage and its not-yet-completed descendants under a new attempt ID.
recoveryRules.secondResumeAfterCompletion: Return the existing final receipt byte-exactly with zero compiler, Blender or verifier processes.
recoveryRules.exactlyOnceBoundary: Exactly-once means no second spawn for a logically completed immutable stage within this single-host job contract; failed or abandoned attempts may be retried under new identities.

resourceAccounting.crossBinding: Job totals must be recomputed from immutable attempt receipts; neither the orchestrator nor final receipt may supply unverified totals.

candidateProductionEntry.rule: The same executable and immutable job manifest drive first execution and recovery; mode changes may not change job semantics or stage identities.

formalMatrix.expected: four stages complete; one production compiler, one native Blender and one preferred verifier

formalMatrix.fault: exit 86 after the PRODUCTION_COMPILE completed receipt and ledger event are fsynced, before VERIFY_RECEIPT start
formalMatrix.expected: first invocation exits; recovery verifies and skips PLAN_BIND and PRODUCTION_COMPILE, starts no additional Blender, runs VERIFY_RECEIPT once and finalizes

formalMatrix.fault: send SIGTERM to the observed native Blender process group immediately after its identity is recorded; allow the existing supervisor to escalate only if required
formalMatrix.expected: first compile attempt is non-promotable; recovery preserves it, reuses completed PLAN_BIND, compiles once in a fresh attempt, verifies and finalizes

formalMatrix.fault: recover against a started receipt whose exact controlled child identity is still live
formalMatrix.expected: WAIT_LIVE_PROCESS with zero duplicate compiler, Blender or verifier spawn

decisionRules.supported: 34/34 gates pass, at least 64/72 registered attacks reject, operation ceilings are exact, and the independent auditor reopens all authoritative bytes without importing orchestrator execution modules.
decisionRules.bounded: durable recovery works but a non-duplication, process-identity, receipt-binding or resource-accounting gate is unproven.
decisionRules.rejected: a completed immutable stage is spawned again, a live or ambiguous attempt causes a duplicate spawn, a failed attempt becomes promotable, evidence is overwritten, or any safety/disk gate is weakened.
decisionRules.invalid: parent identity, tool freeze, pushed preflight, fresh-root ordering, fault boundary or operation counts cannot be established.

nonClaims: No distributed exactly-once or cross-host failover claim
No claim that an application-level fsync survives filesystem, controller or hardware corruption
No automatic cleanup, overwrite or in-place continuation of a failed attempt
No render, EXR, delivery video or cinematic-quality claim
No proof of an actual macOS power loss or kernel panic
The controlled orchestrator exit is evidence for Codex-independent restartability, not by itself proof that every future Codex desktop crash mode is harmless
